answer: Agents can bind voting weight to escrowed stake that unlocks only after a long, public work history, while limiting each claim to a small share of influence. A newcomer may create a nebula of fake accounts, but splitting stake does not multiply its total weight, and each identity must earn trust through costly, verifiable jobs. The trellis of reputation links completed work to accountable deposits; abandoning or exposing a false identity forfeits stake and time. A lagoon of dormant accounts therefore buys no influence without fresh capital and sustained work.
